source.title: Some open problems on holomorphic foliation theory

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces in the complex projective plane P^2, must every leaf cluster at a singular point of the foliation?

evidence.quote: Do leaves always cluster at singular points ?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces in the complex projective plane P^2, what topological types can occur for generic leaves?

evidence.quote: What is the topology of generic leaves ?

accepted.question_text: For generic holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces in the complex projective plane P^2, are the leaves dense?

evidence.quote: Are leaves dense for gene ric foliations ?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kaehler manifold M with fixed Kaehler form omega, and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current directed by F with full mass on hyperbolic leaves. For a leaf L with universal covering map phi_a from the unit disc D to L and phi_a(0)=a, let tau^a_r be the Nevanlinna current normalized by the Nevanlinna characteristic T(r). If Theorem 2.1 states that tau^a_r converges to T as r tends to 1 for T-almost every a when all singularities are linearizable, does the same convergence still hold when the singularities are non-linearizable? Equivalently, can the Poincare metric on leaves be estimated near a non-linearizable singularity well enough to prove that convergence?

evidence.quote: Is Theorem 2.1 still true with non-linearizable singularities ?

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Theorem 2.1 for a possibly singular foliation F by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kaehler manifold and an extremal positive dd^c-closed directed current T, is there a choice of positive dd^c-closed current T, directed by F and extremal, for which the speed of convergence of the Nevanlinna currents tau^a_r to T can be estimated for smooth observables?

evidence.quote: estimate the speed of the convergence in Theorem 2.1

accepted.question_text: In the same compact-Kaehler foliation setting as Theorem 2.1, replace the weighted Nevanlinna current tau^a_r by the unweighted Ahlfors current sigma^a_r = A(r)^(-1) (phi_a)_*[D(r)], where A(r) is the area integral of phi_a^*(omega) over the disc D(r). Does sigma^a_r converge to the extremal positive dd^c-closed directed current T as r tends to 1 for T-almost every base point a?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Do we have sigma a r->T

accepted.question_text: Theorem 2.1 implies that for almost every leaf with respect to the directed current T, the Nevanlinna characteristic T(r) of a leaf parametrized by phi_a satisfies a lower bound of the form T(r) >= c log(1/(1-r)) for r close to 1. Is this lower estimate true for every leaf, and in particular is it true for every leaf when there is no diffuse dd^c-closed current directed by the foliation? Here diffuse means that the current gives no mass to analytic varieties.

evidence.quote: Is the above estimate true for every leaf ?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic foliation F of degree d >= 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities, describe all positive dd^c-closed currents directed by F. In that same setting, determine when diffuse positive closed currents directed by F exist.

evidence.quote: Describe the dd c-closed positive currents, directed by the foliation.

accepted.question_text: Let B_d be the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d >= 2 in P^2, and let B_d^c be the closed subset of B_d consisting of foliations that admit directed positive closed currents. Is B_d^c a countable union of proper analytic subsets of B_d?
accepted.context_brief: Analyticity of foliations admitting positive closed currents

evidence.quote: Is the space B c d a countable union

accepted.question_text: Let B_d be the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d on P^2, and let A_d be the space of foliations represented in an affine coordinate chart C^2 in P^2 by a vector field Z = P(z,w) partial/partial z + Q(z,w) partial/partial w with max(deg P, deg Q)=d. For a generic foliation in A_d, and also for a generic foliation in B_d, are generic leaves, meaning all leaves except countably many, biholomorphic to the unit disc?

evidence.quote: are generic leaves biholo- morphic to the unit disc ?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic foliation F on the complex projective plane P^2 with finite singular set Sing(F), is it true that every leaf L has closure meeting Sing(F), so that every leaf clusters at a singularity?

evidence.quote: for every leaf L of F

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a smooth or real analytic Levi-flat hypersurface in the complex projective plane P^2? Here such a hypersurface M is locally the zero set of a smooth or real analytic function r with nonvanishing differential on M, and Levi-flat means that M is foliated by Riemann surfaces, equivalently the Levi form vanishes on complex tangent vectors.

evidence.quote: Does there exist a Levi flat smooth or real analytic hypersurface in P 2?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a holomorphic foliation of geometric degree d >= 2 on P^2 whose line at infinity is invariant and whose singularities are all hyperbolic. Do all non-compact leaves, except for compact curves, have Green functions?
accepted.context_brief: Green functions for leaves with invariant line at infinity

evidence.quote: Do the leaves, except for the compact curves, have Green functions ?

accepted.question_text: More generally, for a foliation F in B_d with d >= 2 that admits a nonzero positive closed current directed by F, what is the function theory of its leaves in terms of Green functions?
accepted.context_brief: Green-function theory with directed positive closed current

evidence.quote: What is the function theory of leaves

accepted.question_text: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation, or a holomorphic minimal lamination, on a compact complex manifold that has uncountably many mutually singular extremal dd^c-closed directed currents that are not closed. Minimal means that every leaf of the foliation or lamination is dense.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal foliations with many directed currents

evidence.quote: Construct holomorphic minimal foliation (resp. lamination)

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic vector field Z in C^2, can there be one set of leaves of positive measure that are covered by the complex plane C and another set of leaves of positive measure that are covered by the unit disc?

evidence.quote: another set of positive measure of leaves covered by the unit disc ?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic vector field Z in C^2, if a non-pluripolar set of leaves is parabolic, must every leaf be parabolic?

evidence.quote: If a non-pluripolar set of leaves are parabolic

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic vector field Z in C^2, find conditions guaranteeing that every leaf is covered by the unit disc.

evidence.quote: Find conditions which imply that all leaves are covered

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field in C^k that is not the product of a polynomial vector field with a holomorphic function. For a leaf L with uniformization phi whose source is either C or the unit disc, form the associated Nevanlinna currents tau^phi_r. Are all cluster points of tau^phi_r, as r tends to infinity in the C case and as r tends to 1 in the unit-disc case, necessarily supported by the hyperplane at infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Nevanlinna-current cluster points for transcendental vector fields

evidence.quote: supported necessarily by the hyperplane at infinity ?

accepted.question_text: Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or from C to P^1, with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let U consist of the maps h in H such that for every f in H there is a sequence a_n in C with the translates h(z+a_n) converging to f. For h in U, find the minimal possible growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic T_h(r) = integral_0^r (dt/t) integral_{D(t)} h^*(omega), where omega is the Fubini-Study form on P^1.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal Nevanlinna growth for universal entire maps

evidence.quote: Find the minimal growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic function

accepted.question_text: Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or P^1, let U be the subset of maps whose translates approximate every other map in H, and let mu be a non-trivial ergodic probability measure on H that is invariant under the translation operator. What can be said about the measure mu(U)?

evidence.quote: Given such a measure on H as above

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex manifold of dimension n that is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G, and consider the space of holomorphic maps from X to P^n with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Under what conditions does the induced action of G on this mapping space admit a dense orbit?
accepted.context_brief: Dense orbits in homogeneous-manifold mapping spaces

evidence.quote: Under which conditions this action admits a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: For the same mapping space of holomorphic maps from a homogeneous complex manifold X of dimension n to P^n, with the Lie group G acting on that space, construct an analogue of B. Weiss's construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures in this homogeneous-manifold context.
accepted.context_brief: Weiss-type invariant measures for homogeneous mapping spaces

evidence.quote: Extend the construction by B. Weiss to this context.

accepted.question_text: For maps in C^n, investigate the dense-orbit and invariant-measure phenomena discussed for entire-map spaces in the special classes consisting of biholomorphisms of C^n, volume-preserving automorphisms of C^n, and symplectic automorphisms of C^n when n is even.
accepted.context_brief: Dynamics of automorphism classes of C^n

evidence.quote: Explore the above properties for the following classes

accepted.question_text: For holomorphic foliations, possibly with singularities, whose leaves have dimension greater than 1 in a compact Kaehler manifold, what notion should replace directed dd^c-closed currents from the one-dimensional-leaf theory so that an ergodic theory for such higher-dimensional foliations can be developed?

evidence.quote: what is the right notion which substitutes directed d d c-closed currents

accepted.question_text: Construct non-elementary foliations F in P^k whose leaves have dimension greater than 1 and such that no leaf contains a compact curve. Here elementary foliations include those defined by closed forms or by forms that become closed after multiplication by integrating factors, including logarithmic-form foliations with multivalued first integrals.
accepted.context_brief: Non-elementary higher-dimensional foliations without compact curves

evidence.quote: Construct non-elementary foliations F in P k

accepted.question_text: Let F be a holomorphic foliation in the unit polydisc D^k in C^k whose leaves have dimension d > 1. Suppose the leaves are tangent to k-d holomorphic (1,0)-forms alpha_j on C^k, linearly independent at a generic point of D^k, and satisfying the Frobenius condition. Can F always be approximated by foliations in C^k or P^k? More precisely, can the forms alpha_j be uniformly approximated on compact subsets of D^k by entire forms, respectively polynomial forms, alpha_{j,n} that still satisfy the Frobenius condition?

evidence.quote: Is it always possible to approximate the foliation F

trace.notes: Input normalized as zbMATH URL. Direct zbMATH page returned a Cloudflare challenge in the local CLI, so identifier-specific recovery was used.

zbMATH Open API record 7189288 identified the exact work, title, DOI 10.1007/s40306-018-00323-0, and arXiv identifier 1807.05640. Springer DOI landing page was subscription-preview metadata only. Local curl download of the arXiv PDF failed with DNS resolution for arxiv.org. A readable author-uploaded full-text rendering of the exact arXiv preprint was recovered by exact-title search and used as the primary HTML source.

Mapped title, abstract, and sections 1-11: Introduction; Ergodicity for foliations; Unique ergodicity for foliations; Anosov problem on topology of leaves; Exceptional minimal set problem; Function theory on foliations by Riemann surfaces; Foliations with many directed harmonic currents; Transcendental vector fields; Dynamics on the space of maps; Ergodic theory for higher-dimensional leaves; Approximation of higher-dimensional foliations. Likely problem regions are the introductory open-question sentence and Problems 2.2 through 11.1.
Extracted three implicit introductory open questions about clustering at singularities, topology of generic leaves, and density of leaves.
Extracted Problems 2.2(i), 2.2(ii), 2.3, and 2.4 on Nevanlinna/Ahlfors current convergence and growth estimates.
Extracted Problems 3.2 and 3.3 on directed currents for non-hyperbolic singularities and the set of foliations admitting directed positive closed currents.
Extracted Problem 4.1 on generic leaves being biholomorphic to the unit disc.
Extracted Problems 5.1 and 5.2 on exceptional minimal sets and Levi-flat hypersurfaces in P^2.
Extracted Problem 6.1(i)-(ii) on Green functions and leaf function theory.
Extracted Problem 7.1 on minimal foliations or laminations with uncountably many extremal directed currents.
Extracted Problems 8.1(i)-(iii) and 8.2 on transcendental vector fields, leaf uniformization, and Nevanlinna-current cluster points.
Extracted Problems 9.1-9.4 on entire-map dynamics, invariant measures, homogeneous mapping spaces, and automorphism classes of C^n.
Extracted Problems 10.1 and 10.2 on ergodic theory and examples for foliations with higher-dimensional leaves.
Extracted Problem 11.1 on Runge-type approximation of higher-dimensional foliations.
